M/s Moon Light Silk Mills Ltd ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh Shilpa Bank ----- Opposite Party
full_judgment: 4. The petitioners fled written objection denying the allegations and the claims as made by the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank in the petition under' Article 33 of the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank Order, 1972. The petitioners also took the ground that the loan granted by the Government of West Germany was converted into a grant in favour of the Government of Bangladesh. Relief claimed by the Shilpa Bank cannot be covered by the Subsidiary Loan Agreement. The petitioners claim that they are also entitled to the benefit of the said grant. The petitioners also contended that the Bangladesh Government should be made party in this case. The petitioner company has already repaid Tk. 11,60,024.84 including interest against the local currency loan of Tk. 6,50,000 and has also repaid an amount of Tk. 21,69,143.80 including interest against the foreign currency loan which not only covered the dues of the bank but some amount of the same was paid in excess. The petitioners being in darkness about conversion of Foreign Currency Loan into a grant ignorantly executed certain documents regarding rephrasing of loan, etc, by the Bank with the current rate of exchange against each instalment.
